reason: The count is 3–7 secondary veins per side, and the each_side slot points to the leaf midvein (PO_0020139). This matches the text.
'Annual herb, up to 70 cm' gives the height of the whole plant, with an upper bound only.

target: flowers per raceme: many to few (multi- to pauci-)
fix: In paired count prefixes like 'multi- à pauciflores' (and 'pluri- à pauci-'), the first element has a hanging hyphen. Read both as one range from many to few, not just the last prefix.
reason: The racemes have many to few flowers. The annotation keeps only 'few' (from 'pauci'), so the 'many' end is lost.
'Divergent' means the two needles of each fascicle spread apart. 'spreading' (PATO_0104356) on leaf fits.

target: place: along veins (both surfaces) of the expanded calyx lobe (calycophyll) blade
fix: 'pubescent along veins on both surfaces' limits the hairs to the veins. Fill the place slot with the veins, or make the vein the bearer, as in 'on veins beneath'.
reason: The calycophyll blade is hairy only along its veins. Calling the calyx lobe pubescent without that limit overstates it. Also, only the one enlarged lobe is meant, not every lobe.

target: linear-lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate (compound shapes; from = lanceolate with a linear modifier, to = lanceolate with an oblong modifier)
fix: Hyphenated compound shapes 'X-lanceolate' name a lanceolate shape leaning toward X. Map them as one compound value. Do not map the first element to lanceolate (PATO_0001877) and the second to plain oblong (PATO_0000946).
reason: Both ends of the range are kinds of lanceolate. 'oblong-lanceolate' was reduced to 'oblong', which the flora does not say.

target: leaf vein, abaxial side (place: beneath); pubescent, more densely than the upper surface
fix: 'more strongly so on veins beneath': 'so' repeats the quality, and 'on veins beneath' names the part. The bearer is the abaxial veins, not the whole lamina.
reason: This statement puts the denser hairs on the veins of the lower surface. The lamina's own hairiness comes from the earlier clause ('thinly shortly pubescent above').
Thick trunk bark, with the stage set to mature (PATO_0001701). This matches 'of mature trees'.

'Cordate' describes the base by definition, so 'base subcordate' on the leaflet with 'approximately' is fine. The terminal-leaflet position would be better in the position slot, but leaving it out does not make the statement false.

fix: Sentences that start 'Female flowers on ... pedicels' or 'Male flowers: ...' scope everything after them to that flower sex. Fill bearer_whole as was done for 'of staminate flowers'.

Pedicels glabrous or villous: both alternatives are kept as values of pilosity.

A bamboo culm sheath is the sheath of a culm leaf, so leaf sheath shorter than internode is acceptable.

target: 2–3 leaves (min 2, max 3), borne at the top of the pseudobulb
fix: For 'N–M-leaved', 'N–M-flowered' and similar, take the lower bound from the range, not just the number next to the suffix.
reason: The text says 2–3-leaved, but the numbers are [3, 3].
Bracts shorter than calyx: matches the text.
Fruits 'not striped': 'striped' is a synonym of banded (PATO_0001946), and the negation applies to it alone.

The adaxial (upper) surface of the blade has hairs, shorter and sparser than below. Hairy on the adaxial epidermis is right; the comparison is only extra detail.
2 or 3 peduncular bracts read as a count of 2–3 bracts. A peduncle-bract bearer would be more precise.

fix: In 'corolla tube X, lobes Y', the colour after 'lobes' belongs to the corolla lobe, not the whole corolla.
reason: Only the lobes are cream to white; the tube is salmon, pink or white. Mapping cream to yellow (ISCC-NBS level 2) is a loose but acceptable match.
Plants ascending or decumbent at base: both alternatives are kept for the whole plant. 'At base' is part of what decumbent means here.
The upper surface is glabrous, and the midvein is the stated exception. A separate annotation for the midvein covers it, so glabrous on the adaxial surface stays true for the blade surface.

fix: 'fuscous' means dark greyish brown, so map it to brown with a dark modifier, never red. The 'approximately' qualifier is spurious, as nothing in the text hedges.
reason: The bracts are fuscous (dusky brown), not red.
The leaflet blade is oblique and asymmetric at the base, which makes the leaflet asymmetrical. A base position would be more precise but is not needed for the statement to be true.
Petals bear separate oblong glands (Berberis nectar glands), so 'glandular' on petal is fine.

fix: A header such as 'Male flowers:' or 'Female and bisexual flowers:' scopes the following clauses until the next header. Carry it into bearer_whole.

The fig receptacle is mostly not stalked, so negated stipitate on the fig (fruit) fits. 'Mostly' (a frequency qualifier) is not recorded, but that is minor.
